clue.text: Bleak notes requiring immediate attention

parts.note: D and E are two notes of the musical scale
something pressing is urgent, needing attention now

explanation.surface: Grim messages that demand to be dealt with straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something depressing makes the outlook seem gloomy and hopeless, a synonym for bleak.

clue.text: 5 causes the egghead to play up

parts.note: E is the head, or first letter, of egg

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to toy is to play idly

explanation.surface: Something makes the intellectual misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but is the first letter of 'egg'. 'up' turns TOYE round. 5 is ISLE: an EYOT is a small river island.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, so it is a type of isle.

clue.text: Official report concerning revolution

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a turn is a single revolution

explanation.surface: A formal statement about an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is a formal statement filed with authorities, as in a tax return.

clue.text: Less kind, but showing more grit

explanation.surface: Harder-hearted but tougher.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony means hard-hearted and cold, and literally full of stones, so the comparative means both more unfeeling and grittier.

clue.text: 2 is left to the egghead

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run across 'is left' is a coincidence, not a hidden word
E is the head, or first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: Something is handed over to the intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' is the first letter of 'egg'. 2 is EYOT, a river island, and an ISLE is an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, which a river eyot is.

clue.text: Fitting gear, men fidget

indicators.note: to fidget is to move restlessly, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Restless men try on their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or appropriate to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Plan in advance to make change to back row

parts.note: P is a penny, small change
rear means the back
a range is a line or row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Organising beforehand to rearrange the back row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' suggests altering things, but it is coins: P for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To prearrange is to settle the details of something beforehand.

clue.text: Only occasionally is the present connected with the past

parts.note: now is the present moment
and joins one thing to another
then refers to a time gone by

explanation.surface: Musings on how the present relates to history.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from time to time, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Running water or an irregular supply

indicators.note: an irregular supply arrives jumbled, so the letters of the two little words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A water source that may run, or may be patchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular supply' rearranges OR AN. The ARNO is the river through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is running water; the Arno is the Italian river flowing through Florence.

clue.text: The manager is against a man fishing

parts.note: con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
a troller is someone fishing by trailing a line behind a boat

explanation.surface: The boss turns out to be opposed to an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: A controller directs and runs an operation, the job of a manager.

clue.text: Many a criminal has a place in Spain

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
a lag is a convict, an old lag being a habitual criminal

explanation.surface: Lots of crooks are said to have a hideaway in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many a criminal' reads as one phrase, but it splits into M, A and LAG; the second 'a' belongs to the wordplay too.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a port city on the Costa del Sol in southern Spain.

clue.text: A scheming individual, smoother without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the smoother wraps around the point

parts.note: a planer is a tool or worker that smooths wood
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A plotter described as a smooth operator with no sharp edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: the smoother goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plans or schemes is a plotter, someone who organises things in advance.

clue.text: The person responsible for the mail tore stamps off

definitions.text: The person responsible for the mail

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or being out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A post office official rips the stamps from envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmaster is the official in charge of a post office and its deliveries.

clue.text: Short article cannot include European aristocracy, he figures

parts.note: a is the shortest article, the indefinite one

indicators.note: include puts the noble title inside the contracted word

parts.note: can't is the short form of cannot
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A brief piece claims the Continent's nobility is unimportant to a numbers man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he figures' is a cryptic way of saying someone who works with figures, numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant keeps and checks financial records, working all day with numbers.

clue.text: An equestrian recommendation offered in court

explanation.surface: A horseman's advice given to a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on a horse; a rider is also an added recommendation a jury attaches to its verdict.

clue.text: Infuriated by explosion of grenade

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of the weapon apart and they land rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enraged by a grenade going off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be angered is to be made furious, a synonym for infuriated.

clue.text: Taking a drink about four is vital

indicators.note: about means going round, so the drink surrounds the numeral

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Having a pint around four o'clock is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital in its root sense means living, full of life.

clue.text: The gun for a trainee in general

indicators.note: in places the learner inside the word for general

parts.note: rife means widespread or general
L is the learner plate, so a trainee

explanation.surface: Which firearm should be issued to a recruit in the army?
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' suggests an army officer beside 'gun' and 'trainee', but it is the adjective RIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a type of gun.

clue.text: Hit out at soft footwear

explanation.surface: Lashing out at a slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to punch them; a sock is also a soft knitted covering worn on the foot.

clue.text: Edge into church

parts.note: in is a short way of saying into

explanation.surface: Squeezing slowly into a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward is to move slowly a little at a time, which is to inch.

clue.text: Retain a five in sheltered situation

indicators.note: in puts the article and the numeral inside the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Keeping a handful of people somewhere protected.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as held reads 'a few', but A and V are needed, so 'five' was meant; LEE is the side out of the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something as it is means to let it remain, keeping it unchanged.

clue.text: On grassland the right hide's needed

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: Out on the meadow the proper skin is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin, which is what a hide becomes.

clue.text: 22 could be serious

indicators.note: could be shows the letters may become another word when rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 22 across is used as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A number that might be grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the letters of 22 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intention.

clue.text: Move listlessly when one degree under

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Drifting aimlessly while feeling a bit under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one degree under' reads as feeling slightly unwell, which suits the listless surface; the degree is a Master of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is to wander about idly or talk aimlessly, moving without energy.

clue.text: The odd components are sent from the Orient

indicators.note: the parts are odd, that is strange and out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange parts are shipped in from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern describes things coming from the East, the region once called the Orient.

clue.text: Numbers are plainly hesitant when comparatively tight

parts.note: tens are numbers
er is the sound of plain hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Figures show nervousness when things get stretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means taut, so the comparative means more taut or tighter.

clue.text: South African solicitor stayed till the end

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African
a tout solicits custom, selling tickets or business

explanation.surface: A lawyer from South Africa remained to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but it is one who solicits: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out is to remain seated through something to its close, or stay out of a dance.

clue.text: The company go for the Scotch!

explanation.surface: A band of people head off for the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' suggests whisky but means the Scots language, where gang means go.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group or band of people; in Scots dialect to gang means to walk or go.

clue.text: Hard workers, but some can't seem to settle

indicators.note: some means part of the words, so a run is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Industrious types, though some are restless.
explanation.walkthrough: The insects are proverbial for industry; someone with 'ants in their pants' cannot settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are famous for tireless collective labour, so they stand for diligent toilers.

clue.text: Fortunate guy, Steven!-an eccentric

parts.note: he refers to any man or fellow

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Steven, a lucky chap but an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: Steven looks like the person being addressed, but his name is raw material: 'eccentric' gives AVENSENT, and 'guy' is the pronoun for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent arrives as if by divine providence, so it is lucky and timely.

clue.text: The woman in need nags constantly

indicators.note: in shows the name sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A woman in difficulty keeps on nagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Military order to present correct appearance

parts.note: right means correct
dress is outward clothing, one's appearance

explanation.surface: A command to soldiers to look smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Right dress is the parade-ground command for soldiers to align themselves with the person on their right.
